candidates.statement: The primary role of the INDICATIONS AND USAGE section of labeling is to enable health 50 care practitioners to readily identify appropriate therapies for patients by clearly communicating 51 the drug’s approved indication(s). Among other information, the INDICATIONS AND USAGE 52 section states the disease or condition, or manifestation or symptoms thereof, for which the drug 53 is approved, as well as whether the drug is indicated for the treatment, prevention, mitigation, 54 cure, or diagnosis of that disease or condition, including relief of symptoms (21 CFR 55 201.57(c)(2)). Other sections of labeling (e.g., DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION, 56 CONTRAINDICATIONS, WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS, USE IN SPECIFIC 57 POPULATIONS), as applicable, also provide essential details that enable safe and effective use 58 of a drug, and labeling should be considered in its entirety for individual prescribing decisions. 59

candidates.statement: Governing regulations articulate parameters for the evidentiary standard necessary for an 80 indication to be listed in the INDICATIONS AND USAGE section of labeling. For drug 81 products other than biological products, absent an applicable waiver, “all indications listed in the 82 INDICATIONS AND USAGE section must be supported by substantial evidence of 83 effectiveness based on adequate and well-controlled studies” as defined in 21 CFR 314.126(b) 84 (§ 201.57(c)(2)(iv)). 4 For biological products, indications “must be supported by substantial 85 evidence of effectiveness” (§ 201.57(c)(2)(v)). Any statements in this section of the labeling 86 comparing the safety or effectiveness of drug or biological products with other agents for the 87 same indications must be similarly supported – that is, for drugs, they must be supported by 88 substantial evidence of effectiveness based on adequate and well-controlled studies and, for 89 biological products, they must be supported by substantial evidence of effectiveness 90 (§ 201.57(c)(2)(iii)). 91

candidates.statement: The INDICATIONS AND USAGE section should clearly communicate the scope of the 102 approved indication, including the population to which the determination of safety and 103 effectiveness is applicable. The indicated population may mirror the studied population, for 104 example, in terms of patient demographics or severity of disease or condition, but can sometimes 105 differ. In some cases, FDA’s expert reviewers may fairly and responsibly conclude, based on 106 their scientific training and experience, that the available evidence supports approval of an 107 indication that is broader or narrower in scope than the precise population studied. 6 Applicants 108 should discuss the scope of a proposed indication with the applicable review division. 7

candidates.statement: There may also be circumstances in which the indication should reflect the precise population 143 studied. For example, some study designs such as prognostic enrichment strategies (e.g., 144 enrolling only people with a prior myocardial infarction in a study examining the effects of an 145 antiplatelet drug) and most predictive enrichment strategies (e.g., enrolling only people with a 146 specific genomic marker) may identify the population in which the benefits outweigh the risks or 147 the only population in which effectiveness is reasonably likely. 9 In such cases, the indication 148 should reflect only the population studied, unless and until evidence becomes available to 149 support a determination that broader safety and effectiveness can be expected. 150
candidates.context: Conversely, an indication may be approved for a population narrower than that which was 135 studied. For example, a study may enroll and randomize patients, but then stratify participants 136 by the presence or absence of a specific genomic marker. If the study demonstrated benefit only 137 in patients who had tested positive for the marker, FDA’s expert reviewers may fairly and 138 responsibly conclude, based on their scientific training and experience, that the available 139 evidence supports approval of an indication in a population that is narrower in scope than the 140 population that was studied. 8 2. candidates.statement: Generally, the section of the full prescribing information to which particular drug information is 185 most relevant will contain the most detailed discussion of such information. Other sections 186 should discuss only those aspects of the information that are pertinent to those other sections’ 187 scopes and purposes. There may be instances when it is necessary to include information in the 188 INDICATIONS AND USAGE section that is discussed in greater detail elsewhere in the 189 labeling. For example, the INDICATIONS AND USAGE section may include a limitation of 190 use that has a cross-reference to a more detailed discussion of the information supporting the 191 limitation in the WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS section (see section III.B). Because 192 detailed information about topics such as clinical studies and risks related to limitations of use 193 will generally be found elsewhere in the labeling, the information in the INDICATIONS AND 194 USAGE section should be concise. 195

candidates.statement: The INDICATIONS AND USAGE section “must be updated when new information becomes 199 available that causes the labeling to be inaccurate, false, or misleading” (§ 201.56(a)(2)). 15 In 200 addition, it is appropriate in certain circumstances for application holders to update this section 201 to reflect current practices for writing indications for a particular group of drugs (for example, 202 when more information becomes available about the drug, drug class, or specific disease or when 203 the endpoints become better established). Application holders should review the INDICATIONS 204 AND USAGE section regularly to ensure that it reflects current science and, to the extent 205 possible, maintains consistency within a pharmacologic or therapeutic class. 16

candidates.statement: The INDICATIONS AND USAGE section includes the indication and, as appropriate, any 211 identified limitations of use. 17 The INDICATIONS AND USAGE section “must state that the 212 drug is indicated for the treatment, prevention, mitigation, cure, or diagnosis of a recognized 213 disease or condition, or of a manifestation of a recognized disease or condition, or for the relief 214 of symptoms associated with a recognized disease or condition” (§ 201.57(c)(2)). When drafting 215 the INDICATIONS AND USAGE section, applicants should consider what information is 216 needed to clearly convey the approved indication and whether other information in addition to 217 the identification of the disease or condition is warranted. 218

candidates.statement: Limitations of use are presented separately from the indication within the INDICATIONS AND 352 USAGE section (see section III.D.2). A limitation of use is included when there is reasonable 353 concern or uncertainty among FDA’s expert reviewers, who are qualified by scientific training 354 and experience, about a drug’s risk-benefit profile. Limitations of use should be distinguished 355 from contraindications. A contraindication “must describe any situations in which the drug 356 should not be used because the risk of use (e.g., certain potentially fatal adverse reactions) 357 clearly outweighs any possible therapeutic benefit” (§ 201.57(c)(5)). However, there are cases in 358 which the evidence falls short of requiring a contraindication, but suggests that use of the drug 359 may be inadvisable. There are also cases in which there is sufficient uncertainty about the drug’s 360 benefits in certain clinical situations to suggest that the drug should generally not be used in 361 those settings. In these cases, a limitation of use may be appropriate. To avoid redundancy 362 within the labeling, contraindications should not be restated as limitations of use in the 363 INDICATIONS AND USAGE section. 364

candidates.statement: In contrast, information that essentially narrows or further defines a drug’s approved indication 379 and is used to direct appropriate therapy (e.g., identifying particular subsets of the population for 380 whom the drug is approved, drugs to be used only after other drug therapies have failed, or 381 specific tests needed to identify patients to be treated) should be incorporated directly into the 382 indication whenever possible (see section III.A.2).
